name: availability
description:
Check availability of users in Outlook Calendar. Can check the current user's
schedule or colleagues in the same organization by email address.

Both start_date_time and end_date_time must be provided in ISO 8601 format with the user's timezone offset from viewer context (e.g. 1970-01-31T12:00:00-08:00). Always include the offset — never send bare datetimes.

For time-based questions like "am I free at 3pm" or "when is alice available tomorrow",
compute the actual ISO 8601 timestamps for start_date_time and end_date_time rather than
using relative words.

Use this tool to answer questions like:
- "Am I free at 3pm?"
- "When is alice@company.com available this week?"
- "Find a time when both bob@company.com and I are free tomorrow"

The response includes a compact availability string where each character represents a time slot:
0=free, 1=tentative, 2=busy, 3=out of office.

For other people's schedules, event details (subject, location) may be hidden for private events.

start_date_time.description: Start of the time range in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (e.g. 1970-01-31T12:00:00-08:00). Always include the user's timezone offset from viewer context.

end_date_time.description: End of the time range in ISO 8601 format with timezone offset (e.g. 1970-01-31T13:00:00-08:00). Always include the user's timezone offset from viewer context.

schedules.description: Email addresses to check availability for. Defaults to the current user if empty. Can check colleagues in the same organization.

availability_view_interval.description: Time slot interval in minutes for the availability view (default 30, options: 5, 10, 15, 30, 60).
